metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

agent_blueprint.name: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

session.title: porotomo-induced-seismicity: Report the headline results of the agent

answer:
Headline results — run directory /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run, nothing written). All values below are quoted from summary.json in that run directory (generated 2026-11-15T16:02:33+00:00), verified by a read-only inspection of the directory.

SCOPE / RECORDS ANALYSED
- records.analysed = 759 (by_status: {"ok": 759}), stride = 20, spanning 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z; sampled_fraction_of_time = 0.0331; mean 2003.99 ms per record.

ANOMALIES AND DAS DETECTIONS
- Anomalous records: 57 (z_threshold = 5.0). Strongest anomaly zmax = 30.92 at 2016-03-23T20:50:17Z (driver: max_sta_lta).
- DAS detections: 62 events across 53 records; n_scaled_to_full_time = 1870.77; relative b = 0.9849352475487246; relative Mc = -0.8492463451632817; 34 events above Mc.

SEISMOGENIC INDEX Sigma AND P(Mw>=5.5) PER YEAR (calibrated, hazard_catalog_based; catalogue source "GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016", n=5, Mc=-0.48, mag_max=0.07, ML magnitudes):
- b=1.0:  Sigma = -5.448901270028832;  P(Mw>=5.5)/yr at observed rate = 0.00011982478978644906 (~1.20e-4);  P over observed volume = 5.235629034316958e-06.
- b=0.73: Sigma = -5.3193012700288325;  P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004921548824626587 (~4.92e-3);  P over observed volume = 0.00021553767643867072.
- b=0.65: Sigma = -5.280901270028833;  P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.014735103451029574 (~1.47e-2);  P over observed volume = 0.0006483793467004784.

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (hazard_das_upper_bound; b_used = 0.9849352475487246 from "DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE"):
- Sigma = -2.698279919032152;  P(Mw>=5.5)/yr at observed rate = 0.07842182774171746 (~7.84e-2);  P over observed volume = 0.0024076054468051833.

WHICH IS CALIBRATED VS UPPER BOUND
- The calibrated probability is hazard_catalog_based: it rests on the LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 catalogue (GDR 859) with real ML magnitudes (Mc = -0.48, mag_max = 0.07) — the b=1.0/0.73/0.65 rows above.
- hazard_das_upper_bound is a DAS-based UPPER BOUND using uncalibrated DAS relative magnitudes (Aki MLE b from relative magnitudes), so it over-counts and must not be read as a calibrated probability.

ASSUMPTIONS / PROVENANCE
- Read-only constraints honored: no PBS submission, no hazard.py execution, no file writes (jobs.txt/hazard_rerun.log in the directory are pre-existing artifacts of the run, not touched).
- Pumping context per summary.json: source "GDR 917 corrected deployment data".
- Every number above comes from summary.json in the run directory; anomaly/event counts cross-checked against anomalies.csv, events.csv and detect/*.jsonl (765 lines = 759 record lines + 6 retry lines).
